requirement:
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Body prose shares the
containing prose's left edge without added indentation. Each header's badge
is right-aligned and identifies the declaration and its kind.
A narrow colored bar in the right margin delineates the section and uses the
badge's color: blue for requirements, purple for examples, and green for named
definitions. Named definitions use the same badge styling, displaying their
kind and phrase. A square disclosure control at the top of that bar adjoins
the badge without a gap, matches its height, and is separated from it by a thin
border. The same thin divider separates the badge's kind from its name or
phrase. The badge and control form a rectangle with subtly rounded outer
corners and straight internal joins; the vertical bar has rounded ends.
The control shows a minus when expanded and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing
a section hides its body while keeping the header visible. The disclosure
works with a mouse or keyboard.

The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
rationale:
I judged the tests against each clause of `requirements.index.declaration_sections`. I did not read the implementation source. Every obligation maps to a test with real assertions, and I found no gap. The five tests in `src/lib.rs` carry `{test}` references to the subject.

- **Collapsible sections, expanded on open.** `mod[tests]/fn[declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies]` renders a requirement, a nested example and a definition. It asserts exactly 3 `<details class="habeas-declaration"` elements and 3 `</details>`, `<summary>` and `</summary>`. It asserts that each declaration, including the nested one, has the `open` attribute. It also asserts the surrounding prose ("Before." and "After.") sits outside the sections.
- **Collapsing hides the body but keeps the header.** The same test asserts that the header, up to `</summary>`, contains no `habeas-declaration-body`. The body is in a separate `div.habeas-declaration-body`. So the native `<details>` behaviour hides the body and leaves the header visible.
- **Body prose at the containing left edge.** `fn[declaration_styles_distinguish_disclosure_state_and_keyboard_focus]` asserts `.habeas-declaration-body` has `padding: 0`. It also asserts the section margin is `1.25em 0.75em 1.25em 0`, which has a zero left margin.
- **Right-aligned badge that identifies the declaration and its kind.** `fn[declaration_badge_stylesheet_keeps_split_links_in_one_row]` asserts `.habeas-declaration > summary` has `justify-content: flex-end`. The badge markup is asserted in the sections test: kind link and name link, with `aria-label`, `href` and `title`.
- **Kind colors.** `fn[declaration_badges_and_margin_controls_share_kind_colors]` asserts the inline `--habeas-declaration-color` for each kind: req `#006ba8` (blue), example `#7151a1` (purple), definition `#2e8555` (green). It also asserts the `habeas-badge-name` segment is present and that no SVG is used.
- **Right-margin bar.** The styles test asserts the `.habeas-declaration::before` bar declarations: absolutely positioned, `top: 0`, `bottom: 0`, `right: -3px`, `width: 3px` and `border-radius: 2px` (rounded ends). It also asserts the bar's background is the declaration color. It asserts the section has `border-right: 3px solid transparent`.
- **Definitions use the same badge styling, showing kind and phrase.** The sections test asserts the definition header contains the `definition` kind link and a name link showing the phrase `alpha & beta`. It uses the same `habeas-req-badge habeas-badge-name` classes.
- **Disclosure control.** The styles test asserts `summary::after` has:
  - `flex-shrink: 0`
  - the declaration-color background
  - a 1px border with `border-left-color: var(--bg)` as the thin separator
  - `border-radius: 0 3px 3px 0`
  - equal `width` and `height`, and a height equal to `var(--habeas-badge-height)`
  - `--habeas-badge-height: 1.28em`, matching the badge's `1.6em` height at `0.8em` font size
  - `gap: 0` on the summary, so the control adjoins the badge
  - a negative right margin plus `position: relative` and `z-index: 1`, so the control sits over the top of the bar
- **Divider between kind and name, and corner shapes.** The styles test asserts `.habeas-badge-kind` has `border-radius: 3px 0 0 3px`. It asserts `.habeas-badge-name` has `border-left: 1px solid var(--bg)` and `border-radius: 0`. Together these give rounded outer corners and straight internal joins.
- **Minus when expanded, plus when collapsed.** The styles test asserts `content: "+"` on the base `summary::after`. It asserts `content: "−"` on `.habeas-declaration[open] > summary::after`.
- **Mouse and keyboard.** The `<details>`/`<summary>` structure is native. The styles test asserts the `summary:focus-visible::after` outline. It also asserts `overflow-x: auto` and `scrollbar-width: none` on the badge wrapper.
- **Markdown body and nested declarations.** The sections test asserts bold and italic text, a `language-rust` code block, and a nested `<details>` inside the body. It asserts that the nested section closes correctly and that the outer requirement's trailing paragraph stays in the body. It also asserts the `:impl:` option line is not rendered. `fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]` additionally checks that headings and fenced code survive in the body.
- **Header links retained and independent of the disclosure.** The sections test asserts that both links sit inside `<summary>`. It asserts the kind link goes to `#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}` and the name link goes to `requirements-index/rules.{name}.html`. It asserts there is no `habeas-detail-icon`. `fn[declaration_badge_stylesheet_keeps_split_links_in_one_row]` asserts the non-wrapping row. Because the links are separate anchors, they navigate on their own.

I found no unresolved ambiguity. The words "in authored chapters" scope where the rule applies. They do not add a separate behaviour that needs its own test.

:::{req} navigation
Each requirement and example declaration badge has two adjacent links. Its
kind (`req` or `example`) links to the declaration's anchor on the current
page; its full name links to the evidence detail page. These segments stay
together in one non-wrapping row, with no separate arrow link or plaintext evidence link.
Each detail page links back to the declaration's anchored badge and to the
index. Reference badges continue to link to the declaration. These links
resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in
`requirements.cli.mdbook`.
